result.title: Looped GNNs Beyond Fixed Depth: Graph Size Generalization and Parameter-Efficient Adaptation
result.summary: Generalizing from small graphs to larger ones can require computation beyond the depth of a neural model used during training. We study target tasks that admit a common local iterative computation and whose effective dependency radius grows with graph size. The central idea is to learn a local update rule through GNN pretraining, then repeatedly apply the same learned processor beyond the training depth to extend information reach on larger graphs without retraining. Calling such parameter-shared architecture a \emph{looped GNN}, we categorize six schemes for looped GNNs to separate the effects of depth extension, fine-tuning, and freeze-and-steer adaptation. Our analysis establishes fixed-depth information limits and sufficient conditions under which accurate iterative reuse overcomes them. To improve beyond unadapted reuse, we introduce \emph{Loop-Freeze-Steer} (LFS), which freezes the pretrained processor and learns a small controller to steer its repeated application, using much fewer trainable parameters than full fine-tuning. Our finite-sample analysis gives sufficient conditions for adaptation to improve performance on larger graphs. Experiments on synthetic tasks and chip placement evaluate depth extension and adaptation, highlighting LFS's accuracy--trainable-parameter trade-off for size generalization.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究「looped GNN」：先用 GNN 预训练学得局部更新规则，再在更大图上重复应用同一参数共享处理器以突破训练深度，分析固定深度的信息上限与迭代复用条件，并提出 Loop-Freeze-Steer，冻结预训练处理器、只训练小型控制器来引导重复迭代，从而以更少可训练参数改善图尺寸泛化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「参数共享循环迭代扩展有效深度」与 LVR 的 loop/循环 latent 计算、长度泛化及「冻结主干＋轻量控制器」适配思路可能相通，可供核查其信息传播上限与复用条件能否迁移到 VLM 推理状态更新与测试时深度外推。
